evals.name: ask-in-context
evals.prompt: When should our app trigger the iOS camera permission prompt — on first launch during onboarding, so it's out of the way?
evals.expected_output: No — request permission IN CONTEXT, at the moment the user invokes the camera feature, not at launch (HIG Privacy: 'avoid requesting permission at launch unless required to function'). Optionally show a priming screen explaining the benefit before the system alert. Also ensure NSCameraUsageDescription is set.
evals.truth: no — ask in context when the feature is used, not at launch

evals.name: att-priming-violations
evals.prompt: Our App Tracking Transparency priming screen has a big button labeled 'Allow', a 'Skip' link to bypass it, and we keep the content feed hidden until the user opts in. Anything wrong?
evals.expected_output: Three ATT violations: (1) can't label the button 'Allow' or otherwise imitate the system alert — use 'Continue'/'Next'; (2) can't provide an escape hatch that skips the system alert; (3) can't withhold functionality/content or make the app unusable until people allow tracking (no bribing/coercion). All are explicit App Store rejection causes.
evals.truth: three violations: 'Allow' label/mimic, skip/escape hatch, withholding functionality

evals.name: location-when-in-use-first
evals.prompt: Our app shows nearby events. Should we request 'Always' location access up front so background features work later?
evals.expected_output: No — request 'When In Use' FIRST and only what you need; escalate to 'Always' only when background access is core and clearly beneficial (the system later re-confirms 'Always'). For a one-shot need, prefer the system Location Button (temporary access, no full prompt). Don't over-request.
evals.truth: no — request when-in-use first, escalate to always only if core
